claims.text: As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons exhibit grain-boundary disorder.
As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons contain residual stresses.
As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons have limited thermal conduction.
Post-deposition annealing reduces grain-boundary disorder in the films or nanoribbons.
Post-deposition annealing relaxes residual stress and lattice strain in the films or nanoribbons.
Reducing grain-boundary disorder and residual stress enhances cooperative magnetostructural coupling.
Annealing-induced strain relief and reduced grain-boundary disorder decrease local spin disorder.
Decreased local spin disorder enhances cooperative magnetic interactions.
Annealing improves thermal conduction by reducing scattering at grain boundaries.
Improved thermal conduction supports more efficient heat exchange during magnetic-cooling cycles.
Enhanced magnetostructural coupling and more efficient heat exchange produce a larger measured magnetic entropy change.
Enhanced magnetostructural coupling and more efficient heat exchange reduce magnetic hysteresis.
Annealed samples will have a larger magnetocaloric response than the as-deposited baseline under low-field cycling.
Annealed samples will have a narrower hysteresis loop than the as-deposited baseline under low-field cycling.
The as-deposited films or ribbons have diminished magnetocaloric response and broader hysteresis because of surface disorder and heat-transfer limitations.
The annealing effects are expected to be pronounced at applied magnetic fields of a few hundred millitesla.
Very high applied fields may mask the changes caused by annealing.
Very slow cycling may mask the changes caused by annealing.
